small_guidance: The conv_transpose3d kernel uses a gather formulation (each output reads from possibly-valid input positions with stride/pad masking), which is inefficient: with stride=2, only 1/8 of (kd,kh,kw) combos are valid per output, but all 27 are looped. Even keeping gather form, reduce register pressure (currently 80 reg/thread limiting occupancy to 16-50%): try BLOCK_OC=16/BLOCK_SPATIAL=32 with num_warps=4, add num_stages=3 variants for memory pipelining, and hoist the constant id_num/ih_num/iw_num%S checks out of inner loops. Also drop the unnecessary fused_bn_meansub_kernel2 path (it runs after torch BN and just rescales by 1.0, wasting a launch) — fold the mean subtraction directly after BN in a single pass.
large_guidance: Rewrite as a scatter-add: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) loads x[n,ic,id,ih,iw] once, multiplies by the (OC, KD*KH*KW) weight slice, and atomically (or via accumulation in a tile-private buffer) scatters into out[n, :, id*SD-PD+kd, ...]. This avoids the gather's 87.5% wasted work at stride=2 and matches the reference op-count exactly. Alternatively, restructure as im2col-style GEMM where the K dimension is IC*KD*KH*KW with explicit valid masks per output, tiled BLOCK_M=64 over OC, BLOCK_N=64 over output-spatial, BLOCK_K=32, using tl.dot for tensor-core throughput — currently no tl.dot is used so compute throughput is bottlenecked on FMA latency. Fold BN (eval-time scale/shift constants folded into conv weight/bias would violate safety, so instead) and the spatial mean-subtraction into a single epilogue kernel that does one pass: read conv_out, compute per-(N,OC) mean via tl.sum, write (x-mean)*bn_scale+bn_shift. Replace the cudnn BN call with a Triton kernel that uses the running stats directly.
